title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the preceding pages Grothendieck identifies the loop-preserving automorphism group of pi_{0,3} with Sl(2,Z)' = PSL(2,Z) and Gl(2,Z)' = PGL(2,Z). Here pi_{0,3} is the free group on loops l_0, l_1, l_inf with l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1. Inside these groups pi_{0,3} is the kernel of reduction mod 2 (principal congruence subgroup Gamma(2)/±1), with quotient S_3.

The page opens with a remark that is set aside for later. Sl(2,Z) is an extension (he strikes out 'centrale') of the group G_{0,3}. This extension 's'interprète comme T_{1,1}', the mapping-class (Teichmüller modular) group of the once-punctured torus. In modern terms, SL(2,Z) and GL(2,Z) are central Z/2-extensions of PSL(2,Z) and PGL(2,Z), and GL(2,Z) = Out^+(F_2)-type = Mod^±(S_{1,1}).

Section V lists the 'avatars' of one group (PGL(2,Z), with index-2 subgroup PSL(2,Z)):
1) G_{0,3} := Aut_lac(pi_{0,3}). These are automorphisms of F_2 sending each loop class to a loop class, up to inversion. G^+_{0,3} is the orientation-preserving subgroup; G^+_{0,3} = Inn(F_2) extended by S_3 = PSL(2,Z).
2) T'_{0,4} = Autext_lac(pi_{0,4})'. These are outer loop-automorphisms of pi_{0,4} fixing the loop class L_4 and permuting the other three. This is the mapping class group of the 4-punctured sphere stabilising one puncture, which is ≅ PSL(2,Z), resp. PGL(2,Z) in the extended version.
3) The same group as pi_0 of the group A'_{0,4} of homeomorphisms of U_{0,4} = P^1 \ {0,1,inf} fixing the marked point a_{0,4} = 1/2. The orientation-preserving part is A'^+/A'^0.
4) The orbifold (stack) fundamental group of [U_{0,3}/(S_3 x Z/2)], with complex conjugation included, based at -J. Its holomorphic subgroup is pi_1 of [U_{0,3}/S_3]. He says this is described 'à la J. Malgoire'.
5) The orbifold fundamental group of P^1 with weights 0 (cusp), 2, 3 at 0, 1, inf, extended by conjugation. The subgroup is the holomorphic orbifold group Z/2 * Z/3.
6) The triangulated cartographic group Gamma_{inf,3} = <r_0, r_1, r_inf | r_i^2, (r_0 r_inf)^2, (r_1 r_0)^3>, i.e. the extended (2,3,inf) triangle group. Its oriented subgroup is <rho_s, sigma, rho_f | rho_f sigma rho_s = sigma^2 = rho_f^3 = 1> = Z/2 * Z/3, with rho_s = r_inf r_1, sigma = r_0 r_inf, rho_f = r_1 r_0.
7) pi_1 of the moduli of 'universal conformal surfaces of type (0,3)', with the holomorphic version as subgroup. A margin note identifies U^conf_{0,3} ≅ (U_{0,3}, T_{0,3}), hence 7) = 4).
8) T'_{1,1} = T_{1,1}/{±1}. Here T_{1,1} = Autext_lac(pi_{1,1}) = A_{1,1}/A^0_{1,1} is the mapping class group of the once-punctured torus (GL(2,Z)), and the orientation-preserving subgroup modulo ±1 is PSL(2,Z).

A margin adds that the group is also pi~_{0,3}/(l_1^2, l_inf^3) with pi~_{0,3} = pi_{0,3} ⋊ {1, tau}, tau being complex conjugation. This is again the extended (2,3,inf) orbifold group.

Purpose: to assemble a dictionary of the extended modular group in its topological, combinatorial (dessins/cartographic), orbifold/stack and Teichmüller incarnations. This dictionary is needed for the 'équation des lacets' and the Galois/Teichmüller tower program (levels (0,3), (0,4), (1,1)).
errors: In 2) the list of permuted loop classes reads 'L_0, L_1, L_3'; it should presumably be L_0, L_1, L_inf (or the three classes other than L_4). This is a notational slip.

No mathematical errors detected. The identifications are all classical and consistent: PGL(2,Z) = extended (2,3,inf) triangle group = pi_0 Homeo of the 4-punctured sphere fixing one puncture = Mod^±(S_{1,1})/±1.

ideas.where_published: Likely in La Longue Marche (1981, circulated)

ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche / Esquisse (Teichmüller tower) discuss these levels

deep.surprise_reason: This is a well-organised summary dictionary of classical incarnations of PGL(2,Z)/PSL(2,Z): free-group loop automorphisms, mapping class groups of S_{0,4} and S_{1,1}, orbifold groups and cartographic groups. All of it is standard and largely visible in the Esquisse and La Longue Marche. The only mildly distinctive features are the systematic inclusion of the 'conformal' (antiholomorphic) versions and the reference to J. Malgoire's description of orbifold fundamental groups. Neither is a new result.
transcription_corrections: Item 2: the crossed-out line reads 'A'_{0,4}/A^0_{0,4} ≃ Aut(P^1_C \ {0,1,∞})'. 'permutant L_0, L_1, L_3' is probably 'L_0, L_1, L_∞'.

Item 3: should read 'A'_{0,4} ⊂ Aut_top(P^1_C \ {0,1,∞; 1/2} = U^top_{0,4})', with the right-hand note 'sous-groupe des automorph. qui fixent le point 1/2 (a_{0,4} = 1/2)'. The symbol under A'^+/A'^0 is likely T_{0,3} (or 𝔊_{0,3}).
Item 5 subgroup: the divisor is '0·{0}+2{1}+3{∞}', not '2{0}+2{1}+3{∞}'.
Item 4: the group acting is 𝔊_3 × Z/2 (i.e. S_3 × Z/2), with subgroup π_1((U_{0,3}, 𝔊_3), -J) and 𝔊_3 = T^+_{0,3}.
Opening line: 'Ça nous fourmille dans les mains des trouvailles (struck: ?) des Sl(2,Z) ...'. The word 'centrale' is struck out.
